note: THE BRAND, said once. Every page, card and slide takes its colours, type and shapes from here, and the brand page (site/brand/) is built from this file too. A value used anywhere else is a second copy: checks/one_palette.py fails it. Each entry says what it is for and why it is what it is, and checks/brand_reasons.py fails one that does not. A colour that is another colour in a different role says `same_as`, never a copied value.
idea: The look follows the name. Wherefore asks why, so the display face is a literary serif. It compiles, so the page is a terminal's black and anything a person could type is set in monospace. And one bright accent marks the point of a line, the way a passing build does.

ground.why: a terminal's black, faintly cool: the product lives in a shell

surface.role: cards and panels, and what sits on them
surface.why: one step up from the ground, so a card reads as an object without a shadow; what sits on a card is told apart by its border, not a third shade

line.why: visible on the ground and on a card, never louder than text

ink.why: a warm off-white: paper, on a terminal

muted.role: secondary text: captions, labels and fine print
muted.why: for what supports a line, not what makes it; one grey, because a second one nobody could tell apart

accent.role: the one thing to look at: actions, and the point of a line
accent.why: a passing build's green, pushed to highlighter strength. Used sparingly, it means 'this'

on-accent.why: the ground's own black, so the accent reads as a highlight on the page. A role, not a new colour: said as the ground, so it moves if the ground does

caution.role: drafts, and what is still being built
caution.why: a warning that is not an error: nothing is wrong, it is just not finished

fail.why: warm and plainly not the accent, so a failure never reads as a pass

contrast.note: Every text colour on every ground the pages put it on, and the least it must reach: 4.5:1 for body text (WCAG AA). checks/contrast.py computes each and fails one that falls short.

display.why: the literary half of the name: 'wherefore art thou'. Set large, where its contrast has room

body.role: everything that is read rather than looked at
body.why: built for screens at small sizes, and quiet enough to let the serif and the mono speak

mono.why: the compiler half of the name: anything a person could type is set in it

card.role: cards, panels, tiles and the boxes on them
card.why: soft enough to read as an object, square enough to stay a document

control.why: every action is a pill, so anything round can be pressed

wordmark.why: the company's name, set in the display face's italic and never redrawn: until there is a drawn mark, the type is the mark

icon.role: the picture beside the name wherever the company has an account: GitHub, and every social profile
icon.why: the wordmark's first letter, set the way the page sets “compiled.”: the display italic, in the accent, on the terminal's black. One letter still reads at the size of a tab, and every platform crops to a circle, so it sits in the middle with room all round

light.note: THE SAME BRAND ON PAPER. Every role keeps its name - a page says var(--ink) on either ground - and the neutrals invert: the terminal's black is the ink, white is the ground. The accent and the caution keep their values; on paper they are a highlighter, a fill under black type, never type themselves. Only fail changes. gen/brand.py writes these as the map's theme (site/brand/map.css); the app, which will be white, inherits them. checks/contrast.py holds this scheme's own pairs; checks/brand_reasons.py requires every colour to be here, with why.
light.why: The app will be white (owner, 5 November 2026), and the map is read on paper. One brand, two grounds: the terminal by night, paper by day. Black, white and one highlighter either way - on paper the accent marks a line rather than writes it, since lime does not read on white - and only fail is deepened, in its own hue, until it reads as text.

ground.why: white: the app will be white, and the map is read on it

surface.why: the terminal's ink as paper, faintly warm, so a card reads as an object on white without a shadow

line.why: visible on white and on a card, never louder than text

ink.why: the terminal's own black as text: the two grounds are each other, inverted

muted.why: the same cool grey, dark enough to read on white and on a card at 4.5:1 and more

accent.why: the same highlighter. On paper it marks - a fill under black type, the way a pen marks a line - and is never type itself, because lime does not read on white

on-accent.why: black on the highlighter, as on the terminal: text on the accent is black either way, and here black is the ink

caution.why: the same yellow, a fill under black type, as the draft banner already is

fail.why: the coral deepened in its own hue until it reads as text on white: the one value paper changes, because a failure is written, not only marked

contrast.note: On paper the accent and the caution are fills, never text, so no pair puts them on a ground; text sits on them. fail is text, so it sits on the grounds and nothing sits on it.
